parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is sharply split by level. Within this state/province the traveller meets documented, operating protections: statewide public-accommodation and hate-crime coverage, mandatory gender-neutral facilities, a shield law protecting visitors' care access, repealed police-harassment tools, and top-tier protective ranking. But entry and exit remain nationally governed: the passport sex-marker policy, visa case-note tagging, fraud/misrepresentation referral for suspected 'misrepresentation of sex', and documented passport confiscations stranding travellers are universal-exposure measures at the border. National custody, if reached, shows severe documented harm. Working courts that have enjoined some orders are partial mitigation. Severity after outing is moderate-to-major rather than catastrophic; detention at entry is the principal pathway.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport/visa regime: binary sex per birth, X markers stopped, cable instructing refusal where 'reasonable doubt' on sex exists and potential lifetime fraud ineligibility; documented confiscations stranding travellers; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: X passports issued before expiry remain valid; policy challenged in national courts; legal-aid FAQ available.
entry_documents.interaction: State shield law and documents cannot touch federal border adjudication; state protections begin only after entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If detained nationally: corrections bureau conversion-therapy-style policies, hormone removal, immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men; trans-prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several national orders blocked or enjoined; 2020 employment ruling still nominally in force though targeted for 'correction'.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any entry dispute can escalate from document mismatch into national custody governed by hostile rules, bypassing state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National facilities (government-funded single-sex) exclude trans people congruent with identity; ~21+ states/provinces have facility bans, criminalised in 4; one documented arrest of a trans student in a restroom.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state: no facility ban, gender-neutral bathrooms mandated, public-accommodation and constitutional protections in force; shower/ward placement not by birth sex here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Exposure arises only in national or out-of-state facilities; within this state the operative rule is protective.

care_services.exposure: National funding freeze, proposed public-insurance reimbursement ban for under-18 care, hospitals subpoenaed for minors' records; national anti-minor-care framing order.
care_services.protection: State shield law protects patients and providers from out-of-jurisdiction enforcement; city executive order and expanded provider protections documented.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's care is shielded inside the state but uninsured/reimbursability and any federal facility touchpoint remain national.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 'radical gender ideology' framing in law-enforcement guidance; state laws defining sex in ways affecting access.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Framework states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; state police tools (Penal Law 240.37) repealed; panic defence abolished.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Speech/advocacy framing raises general scrutiny climate but no documented targeting of visitors for expression within this state.

minors_guardians.exposure: National executive order framing youth care as 'mutilation'; directive to prosecute facilitators of minors' social transition in national-sphere settings; records subpoenas reach hospitals holding under-19 data.
minors_guardians.protection: State bans conversion therapy, shields youth care and providers from out-of-jurisdiction custody removal and law-enforcement cooperation; anti-bullying protections cover gender identity.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling guardian's child is protected for care obtained in-state, but hospital records and any federal interaction sit under national hostility.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented for this state/province: no trans-specific violence incidents or rates appear in the dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate-crime statute in force since 2019; statewide anti-discrimination enforcement via Human Rights regulations; large trans community infrastructure.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse machinery is documented and operating, unlike many states in the national map.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: how visa-fraud referrals would resolve for a visitor; national/state interaction for healthcare funding; whether passport litigation reverses policy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, injunctions, state shield enforcement and documented advocacy capacity show remedies partially working.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation outcomes can raise or lower exposure without warning; travellers face regime in flux.

anchor_checks.comparison: The national border regime resembles 0.55-B's secondary-screening friction — discretionary refusal, humiliation, missed travel — but adds a documented fraud-ineligibility threat and no near-certain outcome. State-side conditions are far better than that anchor.

Within-state experience matches or exceeds 0.75-C: protective laws actually operating, no facility ban, shield law. But combined regime exceeds it: national custody and passport exposures are documented and harsher than that anchor's brief-detention profile.

Not as low as 0.35-A: no universal exclusion register, no routine denial of entry, no operative imprisonment pathway for mere presence. The passport/fraud regime is a real but discretionary border exposure, and most state-level life is protective.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences two regimes: a strongly protective in-state system (documented shield law, public-accommodation coverage, gender-neutral facilities, hate-crime recourse, repealed harassment tools) and a nationally imposed border/document/custody regime that is the operative exposure — universal document-marker scrutiny, fraud-misrepresentation referral, documented passport confiscation, and severe custody harm if detention occurs. Per the precedence ladder, the worst documented national feature (universal border exposure, tier-1-to-2 custody harms) is partially offset by enjoined orders and functioning courts, while the in-state sphere sits at the 0.75–0.85 level. Averaging the journey stages as one regime yields elevated-reduced risk: materially safer than hostile-tier states, materially below a jurisdiction where the whole journey is protected. 0.70.
